```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from here: into this
# document, and into whatever else needs it, which reads the errata_entries.csv written at
# the bottom of this file rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here, \was{} in an edition. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be
# set by either.
#
# Numbering is APPEND-ONLY once this note is published: an entry can already have been
# cited, so a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved.
#
# claim_ids names the ground-truth rows an entry corrects, semicolon-separated.
#
# form = "note" corrects nothing: it quotes a published claim the 2016 corrigendum withdraws,
# prints no corrected side, and carries the finding in its note.
withdrawn <- paste("“There is insufficient statistical evidence to conclude that indirect",
                   "exposure to information altered legislator behavior.”")

#
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, carrying
# the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence. The sentence already holds
# it, but only inside prose a reader has to parse. Each value comes from the same expression
# that glues the sentence, so the two cannot be written apart, and the gate below re-checks
# that each one is still inside the span it belongs to. An entry of a class that changes no
# quantity carries NA, and so does a note-form entry, which corrects nothing.
# The corrected quantities, one per claim, as plain numbers with an ASCII minus. The same
# value builds the corrected sentence (through str_glue(), with m() restoring the article's
# minus sign for display) and the corrected_values column, so the two are written once.
# Entries 1 and 13 read the deposit's own output. Their sentences print rounded tokens, and
# their corrected_values carry the claims' values.
maintained_output <- function(f) read_csv(here("maintained", "output", f), show_col_types = FALSE)
design_value <- function(tbl, label) {
  value <- tbl$value[tbl$claim == label]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  value
}
n_assignments <- design_value(maintained_output("text_design_parameters.csv"),
                              "Possible matched-pair random assignments")
totals <- maintained_output("text_total_causal_effect.csv")
yeas_corrected <- design_value(totals, "Yea votes in the uniformity trial, corrected")
effect_corrected <- design_value(totals, "Total causal effect in votes, corrected")

cv <- list(
  e1 = str_c(round(n_assignments / 1e9), " billion"), e3 = "0.01", e4d = "-0.250", e4i = "-0.150", e5 = "25", e6 = "15",
  e8d = "-0.425", e8i = "-0.100", e10d = "-0.125", e10i = "-0.225", e13a = sprintf("%.0f", yeas_corrected), e13b = sprintf("%.0f", effect_corrected),
  e15 = "0.01", e16d = "-0.25", e16dlo = "-0.625", e16dhi = "0.2", e16i = "-0.15",
  e16ilo = "-0.35", e16ihi = "0.15", e17 = "0.075", e18 = "0.125", e19 = "0.3", e20 = "0.5",
  e21 = "0.325", e22 = "-0.075",
  e23a = "-0.125", e23b = "-0.65", e23c = "0.2", e23d = "-0.225", e23e = "-0.45", e23f = "0.2",
  e23g = "-0.425", e23h = "-0.775", e23i = "0.025", e23j = "-0.1", e23k = "-0.325", e23l = "0.125",
  e24 = "-0.325", e25a = "-0.37", e25b = "0.025"
)
m <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "-", "\u2212")
ascii_minus <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\u2212", "-")

entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "brief",
  "The number of possible random assignments is restated three orders of magnitude too large",
  "published p. 162",
  "would map each of the [[30 trillion]] random assignments onto just two potential outcomes",
  str_glue("would map each of the [[{cv$e1}]] random assignments onto just two potential outcomes"),

        "$2^{35} = 3.4 \\times 10^{10}$, which the deposit confirms: 35 matched pairs, so",

        "originally.]]"),

  paste("The corrigendum withdraws both claims:", withdrawn, "On the corrected analysis the total",

        "one and a half times as large, and the part of it beyond the direct effect rests on",
        "indirect effects whose confidence regions include zero. The abstract is reproduced as",
        "published."),
  "abstract_effect_twice",
  NA_character_,

  3, "quantity", "pipeline", "brief",
  "Figure 1's upper confidence bound is one grid step too high",
  "published p. 165",
  "The 95% confidence region extends from −0.34 to [[0.02]].",
  str_glue("The 95% confidence region extends from −0.34 to [[{cv$e3}]]."),
  paste("The deposited code reports as each region's upper bound the first hypothesis outside it",
        "rather than the last one inside it, so every upper bound it reports sits one step of the",
        "grid too high; the step is 0.01 here and 0.025 in every other figure. The lower bounds are",
        "correct. Zero lies inside the region on either reading, as the $p$-value of slightly more",
        "than 0.05 at zero says. Entries 15 and 17 to 22 correct the same rule in the appendix."),
  "results_f1a_ci_upper",
  cv$e3,

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

n_notes <- sum(entries$form == "note")
n_corrections <- nrow(entries) - n_notes
n_bounds <- entries |> filter(str_detect(title, "upper (confidence )?bound")) |> nrow()

spell <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten",
             "eleven", "twelve", "thirteen", "fourteen", "fifteen", "sixteen", "seventeen",
             "eighteen", "nineteen", "twenty")
  stopifnot(n >= 1, n <= length(words))
  words[n]
}

# values_in_spans is FALSE where the claim's scale is not the sentence's, under PROCEDURES'
# rule that corrected_values is always on the claim's scale. Such an entry's note must say why.
off_claim_scale <- c(1, 13)
entries <- entries |>
  mutate(values_in_spans = case_when(
    is.na(corrected_values) ~ NA,
    entry %in% off_claim_scale ~ FALSE,
    .default = TRUE
  ))
stopifnot(all(str_length(entries$note[!replace_na(entries$values_in_spans, TRUE)]) > 0))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one expression, so they begin in agreement
# and this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span
# to another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its
# value. Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the
# counts line up, and inside SOME span where an entry marks a label as well as a number and
# its spans outnumber its values.
marked_spans <- function(x) ascii_minus(str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2])

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values), values_in_spans) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, \(v, s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none may
# not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds. A note-form
# entry corrects nothing, so it carries NA whatever its class. An empty claim_ids is stored
# as "" and counts as missing here.
has_ids <- !is.na(entries$claim_ids) & entries$claim_ids != ""
needs_value <- entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note" & has_ids
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[needs_value])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[!needs_value])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | has_ids)
)

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
```

This note lists `r spell(n_corrections)` corrections and `r spell(n_notes)` notes to "Information Spillovers: Another Look at Experimental Estimates of Legislator Responsiveness," published in *Journal of Experimental Political Science* 1(2):159--169, doi [10.1017/xps.2014.9](https://doi.org/10.1017/xps.2014.9), and its appendix.

The article's substantive correction is the 2016 corrigendum, *Journal of Experimental Political Science* 3(2):206--208, doi [10.1017/XPS.2016.8](https://doi.org/10.1017/XPS.2016.8). A coding error in the ideological similarity matrix moved every estimate the article reports from Figures 2 and 3, and the corrigendum concludes that "there is insufficient statistical evidence to conclude that indirect exposure to information altered legislator behavior." This note carries that correction into the article's own text. Each number the corrected analysis changes is corrected; the corrigendum states the corrected Figure 2 estimates, and the Figure 3 estimates, the total causal effect, the appendix's Absolute Distance columns, and its Figure 5 come from the maintained code, which applies the same repair. Each sentence whose conclusion the corrigendum withdraws is reproduced as published and listed as a note, because correcting it would mean rewriting the argument rather than correcting the record.

The remaining corrections have other sources. `r str_to_sentence(spell(n_bounds))` entries correct upper confidence bounds that sit one grid step too high (in one case, two), because the deposited code reports the first hypothesis outside each 95% region rather than the last one inside it; no conclusion the article draws from those bounds changes. Entry 1 is a count stated correctly once and misstated two sentences later. Entry 24 is a lower bound one grid step from the one the deposited code's own surface returns, for reasons not established. Entry 25 is an appendix column whose deposited script sets no random seed, so its published values are one draw that no one can reproduce.

The code supporting the maintained analysis, which reproduces both the article and the corrigendum, is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_2014](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_2014).

```{r render-entry}
# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, which is why every emitted
# entry opens with one. A note prints no corrected side.
render_entry <- function(e) {
  corrected <- if (e$form == "note") "" else str_c("Corrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n")
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ",
      str_remove(e$location, "^published "), ":\n\n> ", bold(e$published), "\n\n",
      corrected, e$note, "\n", sep = "")
}

in_appendix <- str_detect(entries$location, "app\\.")
```

# The article

```{r article-entries, results="asis"}
entries |> filter(!in_appendix) |> split(~entry) |> walk(render_entry)
```

# The appendix

```{r appendix-entries, results="asis"}
entries |> filter(in_appendix) |> split(~entry) |> walk(render_entry)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else
# that needs these entries reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot
# drift.
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
